topic: The scarcity effect: why less feels worth more
title: Why 'Only Two Left' Makes You Want It More
voiceover: Does 'almost gone' make things look better? In 1975, Stephen Worchel, Jerry Lee and Akanbi Adewole tested how supply affects value. A total of 200 female undergraduates rated cookies. One glass jar held ten cookies, another held just two. The cookies were identical, but the ones from the nearly empty jar were rated more desirable. Cookies were also rated more valuable when their supply changed from abundant to scarce. And cookies that were scarce because of high demand were rated higher than cookies scarce because of an accident. It tested one product with one group, so shoppers in real stores may behave differently. So when you see 'only two left', ask whether you want the item or just the scarcity. Tomorrow: why can't you tickle yourself?
